rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to God means coming to Him after death; worldly travel alerts people to the greater journey of the afterlife, as worldly provisions and clothing point to piety.
rows.anchor: وهذا من باب التنبيه بسير الدنيا على سير الآخرة

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali reports his mounting praise and supplication, then the Prophet's similar practice and teaching that God knows only He forgives sins; Tirmidhi grades it hasan sahih, with variant transmission routes noted.
rows.anchor: حديث أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب، رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet praised God, proclaimed His oneness, reclined and laughed, then said God smiles toward a Muslim rider who does likewise; Ahmad alone transmits this report.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عباس؛ أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أردفه

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports the Prophet's riding and travel supplications, including the return formula; Muslim, Abu Dawud, Nasa'i, and Tirmidhi transmit it through routes from Abu al-Zubayr.
rows.anchor: حديث عبد الله بن عمر، رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: أبو لاس الخزاعي
rows.claim: Abu Las reports the Prophet said every camel has a devil on its hump, so riders should invoke God's name, tame it for their needs, and remember God is the one who carries them.
rows.anchor: أبي لاس الخزاعي قال: حملنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم على إبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrator called Abu Las is identified as Muhammad ibn al-Aswad ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: أبو لاس اسمه: محمد بن الأسود بن خلف

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A parallel report says every camel has a devil on its back; riders should say God's name and then pursue their needs without restraint.
rows.anchor: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: "على ظهر كل بعير شيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rhetorical question denies that the polytheists possess prior scripture authorizing their shirk or supporting their practice.
rows.anchor: أي: فيما هم فيه، أي: ليس الأمر كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here umma means a religion; the polytheists have no warrant for their shirk beyond imitating their forefathers, and their claim to follow guidance is baseless.
rows.anchor: والمراد بها الدين هاهنا، وفي قوله:

words: وَكَذَٰلِكَ مَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ فِى قَرْيَةٍۢ مِّن نَّذِيرٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier nations who rejected messengers made the same ancestral-tradition argument; their hearts resembled one another, as another passage observes.
rows.anchor: قد سبقهم إليها أشباههم ونظراؤهم من الأمم السالفة المكذبة للرسل، تشابهت قلوبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In every town where a warner came before Muhammad, its affluent leaders answered that they found their fathers following a religion and would follow their footsteps.
rows.anchor: إلا قال مترفوها إنا وجدنا آباءنا على أمة وإنا على آثارهم مقتدون

words: أولو جئتكم بأهدى مما وجدتم عليه آباءكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if the messenger brought guidance better than their inherited religion, they would reject it because of corrupt intent and stubborn opposition to truth.
rows.anchor: ولو علموا وتيقنوا صحة ما جئتهم به، لما انقادوا لذلك بسوء قصدهم ومكابرتهم للحق وأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God punished the deniers among earlier nations with various torments; they perished while God rescued the believers.
rows.anchor: من الأمم المكذبة بأنواع من العذاب، كما فصله تعالى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes the Qur'an as an honor for the Prophet's people because it was revealed in their language, which they understand best and should follow most fully; the earliest emigrants exemplified this.
rows.anchor: شرف لهم من حيث إنه أنزل بلغتهم، فهم أفهم الناس له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view understands the verse as a reminder for the Prophet and his people; naming them does not exclude others, as other verses show.
rows.anchor: تخصيصهم بالذكر لا ينفي من سواهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will be questioned about the Qur'an and how they acted on it and responded to its call.
rows.anchor: عن هذا القرآن وكيف كنتم في العمل به والاستجابة له

words: أَجَعَلْنَا مِن دُونِ ٱلرَّحْمَٰنِ ءَالِهَةًۭ يُعْبَدُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All messengers called people to worship God alone and forbade idols and rivals, as the mission of every community's messenger confirms.
rows.anchor: جميع الرسل دعوا إلى ما دعوت الناس إليه من عبادة الله وحده لا شريك له

words: وَاسْـَٔلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَآ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid, and also Qatada, al-Dahhak, and al-Suddi, report Ibn Masud's wording asking those to whom messengers were sent; Ibn Kathir says this seems explanatory, not a recitation.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود

words: وَاسْـَٔلْ مَنْ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رُّسُلِنَآ
rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd says the Prophet should ask the earlier messengers on the Night Journey, when they were gathered for him; Ibn Jarir prefers asking the earlier messengers in the first interpretation.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم: واسألهم ليلة الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whatever fruit the people of Paradise request is brought to them; they are secure from its being withheld or running out.
rows.anchor: مهما طلبوا من أنواع الثمار أحضر لهم، وهم آمنون من انقطاعه وامتناعه

words: لَا يَذُوقُونَ فِيهَا ٱلْمَوْتَ إِلَّا ٱلْمَوْتَةَ ٱلْأُولَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception is disconnected and reinforces the negation: the people of Paradise will never taste death there.
rows.anchor: هذا استثناء يؤكد النفي، فإنه استثناء منقطع ومعناه: أنهم لا يذوقون فيها الموت أبدا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report in both Sahih collections says death will be brought as a speckled ram and slaughtered between Paradise and Hell, then each group is told it will have no more death.
rows.anchor: كما ثبت في الصحيحين أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "يؤتى بالموت

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Said and Abu Hurayra report the Prophet's promise that Paradise's people will have lasting health, life, ease, and youth without sickness, death, hardship, or aging; Muslim transmits it.
rows.anchor: عن أبي سعيد وأبي هريرة، رضي الله عنهما، قالا قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that whoever fears God enters Paradise to enjoy life without death, worn-out clothes, or fading youth.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة، رضي الله عنه، قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Jabir reports that the Prophet said people in Paradise do not sleep because sleep is the sibling of death.
rows.anchor: عن جابر، رضي الله عنه، قال: سئل نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أينام أهل الجنة؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iraqis and Abu Ishaq call the transmitter Abu Muslim al-Agharr, while Medinans call him Abu Abd Allah al-Agharr.
rows.anchor: هكذا يقول أبو إسحاق وأهل العراق

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bazzar transmit Jabir's report that Paradise's people do not sleep; al-Bazzar says only al-Thawri narrated it from Ibn al-Munkadir and only al-Firyabi from al-Thawri, though Ibn Kathir notes another route above.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن المنكدر، عن جابر بن عبد الله قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Along with abiding bliss, God shields the people of Paradise from Hell's painful depths; they attain what they seek and escape what they fear.
rows.anchor: قد وقاهم، وسلمهم ونجاهم وزحزحهم من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This great triumph comes through God's favor and kindness, not deeds alone; the Prophet says no one enters Paradise by deeds unless God covers him with mercy and grace.
rows.anchor: بفضله عليهم وإحسانه إليهم كما ثبت في الصحيح

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet urges sound, moderate effort and says no one's deeds alone admit them to Paradise, including him, unless God envelops them in mercy and grace.
rows.anchor: اعملوا وسددوا وقاربوا، واعلموا أن أحدا لن يدخله عمله الجنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made this Qur'an easy, clear, and plain in the Prophet's language, the most eloquent and lucid language, so people may understand and act on it.
rows.anchor: سهلا واضحا بينا جليا بلسانك الذي هو أفصح اللغات وأجلاها وأحلاها وأعلاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though some reject the clear Qur'an, God consoles His messenger, promises victory to him, the prophets, and believers, and threatens deniers; the outcome will confirm this promise.
rows.anchor: لمن يكون النصر والظفر وعلو الكلمة في الدنيا والآخرة

words: تَنزِيلُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ ٱلْعَزِيزِ ٱلْحَكِيمِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent the Book down to His servant and Messenger Muhammad and describes Himself as unconquerably mighty and wise in word and deed.
rows.anchor: نزل الكتاب على عبده ورسوله محمد، صلوات الله وسلامه عليه دائما إلى يوم الدين، ووصف نفسه بالعزة

words: مَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the heavens, earth, and what lies between them for truth, not in vain or falsely, and for a fixed term that neither increases nor decreases.
rows.anchor: إلى مدة معينة مضروبة لا تزيد ولا تنقص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers heedlessly turn away from what awaits them despite receiving a Book and a messenger, and they will learn the consequence.
rows.anchor: عما يراد بهم، وقد أنزل إليهم كتابا وأرسل إليهم رسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols created no part of earth and share nothing in the heavens; all ownership and control belong to God, so the pagans have no warrant for worshipping them.
rows.anchor: أي: ولا شرك لهم في السموات ولا في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks for a revealed book commanding idol worship or a clear proof for this practice; the pagans have no transmitted or rational evidence.
rows.anchor: هاتوا كتابا من كتب الله المنزلة على الأنبياء

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other readers pronounce the word أثرة; Ibn Kathir explains this reading as sound knowledge faithfully transmitted from someone before them.
rows.anchor: قرأ آخرون: "أو أثرة من علم"

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses atharah as someone who transmits knowledge.
rows.anchor: كما قال مجاهد في قوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains atharah as a clear proof or indication of the matter.
rows.anchor: وقال العوفي، عن ابن عباس: أو بينة من الأمر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ahmad reports Ibn Abbas interpreting atharah as writing or line-drawing; Sufyan says he is unsure whether Ibn Abbas heard this from the Prophet.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال سفيان: لا أعلم إلا عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن عياش
rows.claim: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash says atharah means a remnant of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن عياش: أو بقية من علم

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Hasan al-Basri explains atharah as something extracted and brought to light.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن البصري: {أو أثارة} شيء يستخرجه فيثيره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وأبو بكر بن عياش
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash also explain atharah as writing.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، ومجاهد، وأبو بكر بن عياش أيضا: {أو أثارة من علم} يعني الخط

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains atharah as a particular or special part of knowledge.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: {أو أثارة من علم} خاصة من علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says these glosses are close and return to his explanation of atharah as clear proof; he notes Ibn Jarir chose this view.
rows.anchor: وكل هذه الأقوال متقاربة، وهي راجعة إلى ما قلناه، وهو اختيار ابن جرير

words: مَنْ لَا يَسْتَجِيبُ لَهُ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is more astray than those who invoke idols that cannot answer them until Resurrection and are unaware, since they are deaf, blind, inert stones.
rows.anchor: لا أضل ممن يدعو أصناما، ويطلب منها ما لا تستطيعه إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Resurrection the idols will become their worshippers' enemies and disavow the worship, as other passages also say.
rows.anchor: أحوج ما يكونون إليهم، وقال الخليل

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
rows.claim: Mujahid and others take Q as an alphabetic letter like the other disjoint letters at the openings of suras.
rows.anchor: كقوله: (ص، ن، الم، حم، طس) ونحو ذلك، قاله مجاهد وغيره

rows.speaker: بعض السلف
rows.claim: Some early authorities said Q was Mount Qaf surrounding the whole earth; Ibn Kathir rejects this as Israelite fable or fabrication by heretics.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن بعض السلف أنهم قالوا {ق} : جبل محيط بجميع الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir says extensive later tafsir reliance on Israelite books is unnecessary; the license to transmit them concerns only plausible reports, not impossibilities or likely falsehoods.
rows.anchor: "وحدثوا عن بني إسرائيل، ولا حرج" فيما قد يجوزه العقل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim cites an unsound, interrupted report attributed to Ibn Abbas describing seven earths, seas, and Qaf mountains, with successive heavens raised upon them.
rows.anchor: أورد هاهنا أثرا غريبا لا يصح سنده عن ابن عباس فقال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Ibn Abi Talha says Ibn Abbas called Q one of God's names.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ق} قال: هو اسم من أسماء الله، عز وجل

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir confirms Mujahid's view that Q is an alphabetic letter, which distances the mountain story from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: والذي ثبت عن مجاهد: أنه حرف من حروف الهجاء، كقوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An unnamed view expands Q as the omitted phrase "the matter is decided by God," but Ibn Kathir objects that no clue signals this ellipsis; the cited poem does not solve that problem.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد "قضي الأمر والله"، وأن قوله: {ق} دلت على المحذوف من بقية الكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majestic Qur'an is noble and great, impervious to falsehood from before or behind, and sent down by the Wise and Praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: أي: الكريم العظيم الذي لا يأتيه الباطل من بين يديه ولا من خلفه

rows.speaker: بعض النحاة
rows.claim: Some grammarians, as Ibn Jarir reports, take verse 50:4 as the explicit answer to the oath.
rows.anchor: فحكى ابن جرير عن بعض النحاة أنه قوله: {قد علمنا ما تنقص الأرض منهم وعندنا كتاب حفيظ}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers the implicit answer in the ensuing message: establishing prophethood and resurrection; Qur'anic oaths often work this way, as in another sura.
rows.anchor: بل الجواب هو مضمون الكلام بعد القسم، وهو إثبات النبوة، وإثبات المعاد

words: بَلْ عَجِبُوٓا۟ أَن جَآءَهُم مُّنذِرٌۭ مِّنْهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers marvel that a human messenger came from among them, but this is no marvel because God chooses messengers from angels and people, as another verse says.
rows.anchor: تعجبوا من إرسال رسول إليهم من البشر كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask how they can return to their former bodily form after death, decay, severed limbs, and becoming dust; they regard resurrection as impossible.
rows.anchor: وتقطعت الأوصال منا، وصرنا ترابا، كيف يمكن الرجوع بعد ذلك إلى هذه البنية والتركيب

words: قَدْ عَلِمْنَا مَا تَنقُصُ ٱلْأَرْضُ مِنْهُمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what earth consumes from their bodies and where every part disperses; His preserving record contains and records all things.
rows.anchor: ما تأكل من أجسادهم في البلى، نعلم ذلك ولا يخفى علينا أين تفرقت الأبدان
